The database backup screen exports, restores and deletes only backup tables this plugin created — other tables can no longer be named in those requests. And markup the plugin generates is filtered through an explicit allowlist as it is printed, replacing places that trusted the output to have been escaped earlier.
documents.s: Permissions now check the record, not just the role

documents.t: Uninstall used to stop partway through. With "delete all data on uninstall" switched on, removing the plugin still left tables, scheduled jobs and taxonomy terms behind. The backups screen could go blank. Any .sql file in the backup folder without a matching database record caused a fatal error while the list was being built. Backups are now written under your uploads folder instead of directly into wp-content; backups taken by earlier versions stay listed, restorable and deletable — nothing is moved or lost. Vehicle quick edit accepted values the full editor rejects. A daily price could be saved as a negative number, which then multiplied into rental totals; the seat count could be zero or above the configured maximum. Log retention settings were ignored. "Auto Cleanup Logs" and "Log Retention (Days)" had no effect: the daily purge always deleted entries older than thirty days, permanently, even with cleanup switched off or retention set higher. Saving the Vehicle settings tab silently reset two Frontend fields — "Vehicles per page" and "Default sort order" — that the Vehicle tab does not even display. The dashboard's recent-bookings panel could sit up to twelve hours out of date, because its cache was cleared under a name the cache no longer used. The customers screen re-ran its full query set on every load for the mirror-image reason: it requested a cache type that had never been registered, so nothing was stored or read. Search could be asked to render the whole fleet. Vehicle search accepted any page size; search and testimonials now cap it at the limit their own settings advertise. The translation catalogue now compiles without errors — strings containing placeholders like %days% were being mis-flagged as printf formats.
Both screens have been rebuilt. Vehicle Settings opens in the new layout by default; adding ?ui=legacy to the page URL brings back the previous one for this release.
documents.s: New: redesigned Dashboard and Vehicle Settings

documents.t: Temporary cache entries, the last-login record, background job names and the JavaScript objects the admin screens read now all carry the plugin's own prefix, so they cannot collide with another plugin storing something under the same name. Every script and stylesheet is registered under its full prefix too — WordPress keeps whichever was registered first under a shared short name and discards the other without warning. Around 2,000 lines of code that nothing referenced were removed, including a file registering database-maintenance commands and one that would have exposed protected vehicle and booking fields over the REST API had it ever been switched on.

No action required. Administrators are unaffected by the permission changes; on sites with editor or author roles, those users can now only act on records they are entitled to. Settings belonging to the removed controls are cleaned up for you.

A patch release about honesty. The dashboard chart was named after something it does not measure, and a set of admin strings was being shipped in English despite having been translated months ago. Both are fixed — and the second one turned out to have a cause worth writing down. Written before 6.0.0 This post is the record of a release that shipped before 6.0.0, which renamed the plugin's post types, taxonomies, options, meta keys and hooks. The identifiers below are the names those versions actually used, and they are kept that way on purpose. For the current names — and a conversion table — see the 6.0.7 release post.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.1 / Pro v5.2.1 — A chart that says what it counts, and translations that ship

documents.t: The dashboard's bar chart was labelled "Revenue (Last 7 Days)". It sums _mhm_total_price for confirmed and completed bookings, bucketed by DATE(post_date) — the date each booking was created. That is not rental income earned in those seven days; it is the value of new business booked in them. The mismatch was visible: the table directly beneath the chart lists bookings by pickup date. So a rental company with a full week ahead could see a row of upcoming rentals under a chart reading zero, and reasonably conclude the chart was broken. It wasn't — it was answering a different question than its title asked. The label now reads "New Bookings Value (Last 7 Days)", and the daily series is "Daily Bookings Value". The numbers have not changed. We deliberately did not move the chart onto pickup dates, because post_date is the basis shared by the dashboard metrics, the period deltas, the booking statistics, the deposit statistics and the comprehensive report. Changing only the chart would have left the plugin with two different definitions of "revenue" on one screen. Reporting on realised rental income is a genuine feature, and it belongs in its own release rather than smuggled into a label fix.
documents.s: The chart was measuring the right thing under the wrong name

documents.t: WordPress serves JavaScript translations from one JSON catalogue per script, named after an MD5 of the script's path. Those catalogues are generated by wp i18n make-json, which — by default — only looks at references ending in .js or .min.js. Every React reference in our translation template is a .jsx source path. So the command matched nothing, printed a success line, and wrote no React catalogues at all. Because regeneration correctly runs with --no-purge, the previous catalogues survived untouched, and the check that was supposed to catch this only asserted that the files existed. They did. They were four months old. The result: "Pending Payments", "Upcoming Operations", their empty-state messages, and the notice shown when an admin screen fails to load were all translated in the catalogue and all displayed in English. This release fixes the build and, more importantly, changes what the check actually checks. It now compares the shipped catalogues against the translation source on three axes — the script each catalogue claims to belong to, whether this run actually rewrote it, and whether every string the source assigns to that screen is present. It runs on every push. A green result now means something.
documents.s: Five translated strings that never reached anyone

documents.t: The paid add-on's five React screens — Reports, Messages, Export, Vendor Management and Vendor Reports — had been shipping entirely untranslated since they moved into their own plugin. The sources had been corrected to the add-on's own text domain at the time, but nothing rebuilt the compiled bundles, because the build configuration had not moved with them. That chain is now closed end to end: the bundles are rebuilt against the right text domain, the translation template scans the React sources, 325 strings are translated, and the catalogues are generated under the names WordPress actually resolves. All five screens were verified in a browser in Turkish before this release, tab by tab. Pro v5.2.1 also corrects its declared minimum Lite version. The translation fix depends on a parameter Lite gained in this release; with an older Lite the add-on does not fail, the screens simply stay English.
documents.s: Pro: the same class, five screens wide

documents.t: Eleven translation catalogues belonging to screens and blocks that are no longer part of the free plugin were removed. Nothing loaded them. The readme's bundled-library inventory now lists Chart.js 4.5.1 alongside flatpickr and Swiper, with its licence and upstream source. It is compiled into the dashboard bundle rather than shipped under assets/vendor/, and that distinction is stated.
Nothing to do. No figure, setting or stored record changes. Update both plugins together if you run the paid add-on.

A patch release with one uncomfortable admission in it. Preparing for the WordPress.org submission, we ran our WooCommerce control checklist against the whole codebase for the first time — and found that we had never answered WooCommerce's compatibility questions at all.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.2 / Pro v5.2.2 — What we tell WooCommerce, and one thing we were telling it wrong

documents.t: WooCommerce asks every plugin that touches orders to declare which of its newer features it works with. A plugin that says nothing is filed as uncertain, and the site owner is warned by name when they try to switch on High-Performance Order Storage — which has been the default for new stores since WooCommerce 8.2. We had never declared anything. Not "incompatible" — nothing at all.

A compatibility declaration is a promise, and a false one is worse than silence: people enable HPOS on the strength of it and lose data quietly. So we checked rather than assumed. Every order this plugin touches is read through wc_get_order(); there is no post-meta access keyed to an order id; nothing queries wp_posts or shop_order for orders; no order is created or updated with wp_insert_post(). That is now declared, in both the free plugin and the paid add-on.
documents.s: HPOS: compatible, and measured before saying so

documents.t: This is the part worth reading if you run a store. We could have stayed quiet. Instead we checked what actually happens on a block-based checkout, and declared incompatible, because that is the truth: The payment-type selector, the custom tax row and the return-to-cart link never render — they are printed from classic-checkout hooks the block checkout does not run. The availability check does not run. woocommerce_checkout_process is where we verify that the vehicle is still free for the requested dates. On a block checkout that hook never fires, which leaves a window where two customers can book the same vehicle for the same dates. If your store uses the block checkout, switch to the classic checkout while using this plugin. Making the block checkout genuinely supported means rebuilding those surfaces on the Additional Checkout Fields API and a Store API integration — a feature, not a flag, and one we would rather do properly than claim.
documents.s: Block cart and checkout: not compatible, and we say so

documents.t: The payment type chosen at checkout was written with update_post_meta( $order_id, … ). Under HPOS an order is not a post, so that writes a row keyed to something that is not the order. It now goes through WooCommerce's own order object. On a store that has not switched to HPOS, that object writes to post meta anyway — so the value stays exactly where it has always been. Nothing is moved and nothing needs migrating.
documents.s: One value was being stored where HPOS cannot read it

documents.t: The independent audit we run before every release build caught a claim inside this very change that a search disproves. Our first draft of the add-on's explanation said it "registers no checkout hooks and prints nothing into cart or checkout". It does both — four hooks, in two files. The audit also did the work we had skipped: it read WooCommerce's own source and established that the Store API does run two of those hooks, so most of that surface survives a block checkout, and only the cart line-item name is classic-only and cosmetic. That mixture is neither "compatible" nor "incompatible", so the add-on declares neither and explains why. We are writing this down because the correction is the useful part. A release note that only lists what went right teaches nobody anything, least of all us.
Nothing to do. Update both plugins together if you use the paid add-on.
Another patch on the way to the WordPress.org submission, and another release where the interesting part is not the bug we fixed but what we found while checking whether we had described it honestly.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.3 / Pro v5.2.3 — A table WordPress was never really looking at, and a privacy notice that named the wrong things

documents.t: WordPress has a function, dbDelta(), that takes a CREATE TABLE statement and works out the difference between it and the table you already have — adding columns you have introduced since the last release, without touching the data already in them. It is how a plugin evolves its own schema safely. It does not execute the statement. It parses it. And the way it finds the table's name is to take the first thing after the words CREATE TABLE. Our background-job table was created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. So dbDelta() had been tracking, for as long as that table has existed, a table called IF. The table itself was fine — the database executed the raw statement correctly and always had. Nothing was lost, and nothing is wrong on your site today. But dbDelta() runs DESCRIBE against the name it parsed, DESCRIBE IF fails, and a table it cannot describe is skipped entirely. Any column we added to that table in a future release would have been silently ignored: no error, no warning, dbDelta() reporting success while doing nothing. We measured it rather than reasoning about it. Adding a column to the schema and re-running the migration before the fix: the column was not created. After the fix: it was. The same defect was in two more CREATE TABLE statements in the paid add-on. One of them — the reports background-job table — is created on activation and genuinely had the problem. The other belongs to a monitoring subsystem that nothing currently starts; we fixed it anyway so both read the same way, and we would rather say that plainly than let a changelog imply we repaired something that was never running.
documents.s: The table update that could never have landed

documents.t: The readme's Privacy section is the part of a plugin page that a site owner copies into their own privacy policy. Ours said that every booking record stores the visitor's IP address and browser user-agent. That turned out to be almost exactly backwards. The code that writes an IP onto a booking sits behind an endpoint that nothing in the plugin posts to. The real booking flow — the form, the cart, WooCommerce checkout — records no IP at all. So the one store we disclosed was the one that, in practice, barely exists. Meanwhile three that do exist were not mentioned: The contact form. Every submission is kept with the sender's name, e-mail, telephone, company, the message, a link to any file they attached, and the IP and user-agent it came from. There is no retention setting on these records and nothing ever deletes them. The attached file goes to your ordinary uploads folder, reachable by anyone with the URL, and stays there even if you delete the message. The rating form. Reviews are stored as ordinary WordPress comments, so WordPress itself records the reviewer's IP and user-agent — as it does for any comment. Guest reviews are reachable through Tools → Erase Personal Data, which matches comments by e-mail address. A review left by a logged-in customer is saved against their user ID with no e-mail on the comment, so those tools will not find it; you have to delete it from the Comments screen. The e-mail log. Alongside the recipient and subject, it keeps the booking details each message was built from — customer name, contact details, rental dates. Not the assembled message body. It has its own retention setting, 30 days by default. The activity log, which we had described correctly, keeps IP, user-agent and user ID per entry on a configurable retention, also 30 days by default. Nothing about what the plugin stores has changed in this release. What changed is that the description of it is now true. If you have a privacy policy that was written from our old text, it is worth re-reading it against the new section.
documents.s: The privacy notice, rewritten because it was wrong

documents.t: None of this came out of the fix. It came out of putting the fix in front of an independent model and asking it to disprove our own description, five times over. Each round found something in the text we had just written to correct the previous round: a list read as a delete-list when it was a keep-list; a test's normalised key names mistaken for the real ones; a count of ten where the code has a hundred and sixty-one. The pattern in every one of them was the same — assuming what something meant instead of reading it. That is worth naming publicly, because it is the failure mode that produces confident, well-written documentation that happens to be false, and a privacy notice is exactly the kind of document where that does real harm. The same rounds turned up a scratch file that had been shipping inside our release ZIPs since 5.2.1. The build now holds an allow-list of what may sit in the archive root and refuses to build otherwise, because the exclusion list we had could only ever catch the files somebody had thought of.
documents.s: How we found it, which is the part worth writing down

documents.t: Nothing to do. There is no pending column for the corrected table, so nothing changes on your site on update; the fix is what makes the next schema change actually apply. Pro 5.2.3 ships alongside and requires Lite 5.2.3.
A small release with a simple theme: fitting into WordPress rather than competing with it.
documents.s: Rentiva v5.2.4 — The menu moves down, and every link out of your site is now written down

documents.t: MHM Rentiva registered its top-level admin menu at position 58, which put it directly above Appearance — ahead of most of WordPress's own items. That is a prominent spot, and on a site running several plugins it is exactly how the admin sidebar turns into a scramble. It now sits at 76: still top-level, but below Appearance, Plugins, Users and Tools, immediately above Settings. Nothing else changed — the same screens are underneath it in the same order. If you navigate by muscle memory, this is the one thing you will notice.

The readme said the plugin uses no external services. That is true in the sense that matters — it makes no HTTP request to anyone, sends nothing about your site or your customers anywhere, and loads every asset including its webfont from your own server. But the admin screens do contain ordinary hyperlinks, and a reader checking the claim would find them and reasonably wonder. So the "External services" section now lists them: the documentation site, the issue tracker, wpalemi.com with its terms and privacy pages, this plugin's WordPress.org support forum, the two SMTP plugin pages the setup wizard suggests, and a YouTube channel. They open only if you click them, and they send nothing when you do.

The same section previously said that a check in our build "fails if a request to any third-party host is introduced." That was not true, and the file it referred to says so itself, in a comment we wrote: "this gate cannot catch a NEW third-party host nobody has thought of. It is a regression fence, not a discovery tool." It is a list of sixteen specific hosts — the geolocation, CDN, analytics and Gravatar services earlier versions used — and it scans PHP only. We confirmed the gap by testing it: a request to one of those sixteen fails the build, a request to a host nobody listed passes. So the readme now describes the check as what it is. The underlying claim — that the plugin makes no third-party request — still holds and was verified by sweeping the shipped code, not by trusting the gate. We are writing this down publicly because it is the third time in two releases that a sentence of ours turned out to be an assumption rather than a measurement, and the pattern was identical each time: reading a thing's name instead of reading what it does.
documents.s: A sentence we had to take back

documents.t: Nothing to do.
MHM Rentiva is now published on the WordPress.org plugin directory. You install it the way you install anything else — search for it, click install — and WordPress keeps it updated from there on.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.0.7 — MHM Rentiva is now on the WordPress.org plugin directory

documents.t: Until today the plugin reached you as a ZIP file you had to receive, upload and re-upload on every update. That is no longer the route: In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New. Search for MHM Rentiva. Click Install Now, then Activate. The listing lives at wordpress.org/plugins/mhm-rentiva. From here on, updates arrive the same way every other directory plugin's updates arrive — WordPress checks on its own schedule and offers the new version on your Plugins screen. Nothing to download by hand. Uploading a ZIP still works, and remains the way to install a specific build rather than the current release — for example a version from the GitHub releases page. The installation guide now describes all three routes. WooCommerce is still required, and is checked when the plugin activates.
documents.s: Installing has changed, and it is simpler

documents.t: WordPress.org's review of the plugin found one issue, and 6.0.7 is its fix. A batch customer-update method in the customer performance helper wrote WordPress user accounts behind the blanket edit_users capability — without asking whether the caller may edit that particular account, or whether the account was one this plugin manages. It had no caller anywhere, in this release or any earlier one, and there was no screen or address through which it could be reached. It was removed rather than repaired, because unreachable code that writes user accounts should not ship at all. The two places that do edit an existing customer — the customer edit screen and the delete route — already asked that per-account question beside the write, and still do. Adding a customer is a different case: it creates the account, so there is no existing account for such a question to be about, and it is gated on the permission WordPress itself requires to create a user.

The last release written about here was 5.2.4. Between it and today sits 6.0.0, which was a major release with breaking changes — and they are the silent kind. If you have custom code that hooks into this plugin, it will simply stop running after the update: no error message, nothing in the log, the customisation just quietly stops happening. 113 hooks were renamed. To convert your own code, apply these two steps in the order given, because the order matters: In the older slash-style names, replace every / with _: mhm_rentiva/testimonials/limit becomes mhm_rentiva_testimonials_limit. Then replace the prefix mhm_rentiva_ with mhmrentiva_: that name finishes as mhmrentiva_testimonials_limit. Doing step 2 first produces names that do not exist. Two hooks used a bare mhm_ prefix and follow the same idea: mhm_message_created and mhm_message_status_changed become mhmrentiva_message_created and mhmrentiva_message_status_changed. The post types and taxonomies were renamed too, which changes the WordPress core hooks built from them — this is the part most easily missed, because these are not our hook names. save_post_vehicle is now save_post_mhmrentiva_vehicle, and the same applies to add_meta_boxes_* and to the manage_*_posts_columns / manage_*_posts_custom_column pairs. The renames are: Old New vehicle mhmrentiva_vehicle vehicle_booking mhmrentiva_booking vehicle_addon mhmrentiva_addon mhm_app_log mhmrentiva_app_log mhm_email_log mhmrentiva_email_log mhm_contact_message mhmrentiva_contact vehicle_category mhmrentiva_vehicle_category addon_category mhmrentiva_addon_category The same rename affects any query you wrote by hand. A WP_Query with 'post_type' => 'vehicle', a pre_get_posts handler that checks for it, a get_posts call, a shortcode of your own — all of these now match nothing, silently, because they ask for a post type that no longer exists under that name. What to search your custom code for before updating: mhm_rentiva, mhm_message_, save_post_vehicle, and the quoted literals 'vehicle', 'vehicle_booking', 'vehicle_addon' and 'vehicle_category'. Your stored data is moved to the new names by a migration that runs once, automatically, the first time you load the admin after updating. Nothing is deleted and nothing needs to be re-entered. If you also run the paid add-on, update both at the same time: this version refuses to migrate underneath an older add-on rather than leave your data half-moved.
documents.s: Coming from 5.x? Read this before you update

documents.t: If a customer paid and then cancelled, Rentiva marked the booking as awaiting a refund and stopped there. No money moved. Somebody had to notice and refund it by hand. From 6.1.0 the cancellation carries the refund through to your payment gateway itself.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.0 — Cancelling a paid booking now returns the money

documents.t: This applies to both ways a booking gets cancelled: the customer cancelling their own booking, and you cancelling it from the deposit screen. Both now run the refund to the end. Where the gateway can return the money, it does, automatically. Where it cannot — an offline payment, a gateway that does not support refunds — the booking is recorded as awaiting a manual transfer, and the customer is told that a person will transfer it rather than being promised an automatic return that is not coming. Which of the two happened is written on the booking and stated in the e-mail the customer receives. A customer who cancels before the cancellation deadline now gets the whole refundable balance back automatically, with no step from you in between. Rentiva defines no cancellation fee, so a full refund is the only policy it can apply.

While fixing the path above, a number of related faults came out. All of these are fixed in 6.1.0: Refunding a paid order failed. The refund screen refused any order that had actually been paid. It was asking whether WooCommerce still considered the order editable — which is only true while an order is pending, on-hold or a draft — instead of asking whether the gateway could send the money back. A deposit booking's second order was invisible to refunds. When a booking was paid in two parts, the remaining-payment order was not found at all, so only the deposit came back. One refund was counted twice. A single refund ran through two separate record-and-notify steps, so the booking's refunded total was doubled and the customer received two e-mails for it. The refund notice did not always reach the customer. It read an e-mail field that the contact form fills in and bookings do not. When that field was empty it skipped the notice silently. It now looks where the rest of the plugin looks: the booking's own customer e-mail, then the WooCommerce billing address, then the linked account. A refund nobody's gateway performed was recorded as completed. It is now recorded as awaiting a manual transfer, because the money has not moved until someone moves it. A part-card, part-cash refund told you to transfer the whole amount by hand. The two amounts are now named separately: what the gateway already returned, and what still has to be transferred. Cancelling one order on a two-part booking disturbed the other. Cancelling the unpaid remaining-payment order used to cancel or demote the whole booking even though the deposit order had been paid — with no refund anywhere. The paid order is now left alone, the dead order's link is cleared so you can issue a fresh payment link for what is still owed, and you are notified. Manually created bookings had no payment method at all, which left them unlabelled in the booking list and its filter, refused by the refund path, and grouped into a blank bucket in payment-method reports. They are now recorded as offline payments. The refund box on the booking screen shows its form for offline bookings with a balance — for the first time. The box was always there; in place of the form it printed "No refundable payment found for this booking," because the form needed a figure that nothing ever wrote. Two refunds started at the same moment on the same booking — a cancellation and one you started from the admin screen — can no longer run at once.
documents.s: Several things that made refunds unreliable

documents.t: Rentiva converts between your currency and its smallest unit. It used to assume that unit was always one hundredth. It now reads your store's own setting: WooCommerce → Settings → General → Currency Options → Number of Decimals. If your store uses the default of two decimals, nothing changes for you. If your store is set to a different number of decimals, read this before updating: refund and payment amounts that Rentiva recorded before this release are re-read at the new scale rather than converted. There is no migration step for existing records, and none is planned. Currencies without minor units — the Japanese yen, for example, at zero decimals — are the case this affects.
documents.s: Money conversion now follows your store's decimals

documents.t: If a booking's deposit was taken outside WooCommerce, Rentiva no longer offers a WooCommerce payment link for the remaining balance. For a manually created booking that never had a WooCommerce order, that link always failed anyway. For a booking that started at WooCommerce checkout and whose deposit was later marked as received offline, the link did work — and that was the fault: completing it built a WooCommerce order that quietly erased the earlier offline deposit from the booking's recorded paid amount. The deposit screen now explains the situation instead of offering a button that would lose money. Process Remaining Amount, which records the balance as settled without going through WooCommerce, is unaffected and still works.
The vehicles list is rebuilt, with list, card and calendar views. There is a new monthly fleet occupancy calendar showing every vehicle's month at a glance. The Additional Services screen is new.

Rentiva is on the WordPress.org plugin directory, so the update appears on your Plugins screen on WordPress's own schedule — usually within half a day. You can also check for it immediately from Dashboard → Updates. Tested up to WordPress 7.1. Requires WordPress 6.7 and PHP 8.1.

If your vehicle detail fields were configured before 6.1.2, adding gallery images and pressing Update could wipe the gallery you had just added. 6.1.3 stops that, and it asks nothing of you: no database change, no re-saving of settings. Installing it is enough.

Two boxes that were never real fields — an empty Image and an empty Gallery Images — sat in the Vehicle Details grid on every vehicle screen. They looked cosmetic. They were not: the second one carried the same form field name as the gallery itself, and when two fields on a page share a name, the browser sends both and the last one wins. The empty box came last, so pressing Update wrote nothing over the gallery you had just uploaded. 6.1.2 stopped new sites from ever reaching that state, but it did nothing for sites already in it — and that is most sites that had saved their vehicle settings at least once. The reason it survived is worth one sentence: the code that decides which fields exist would invent a label for any name it did not recognise, and an invented label made an unrecognised name look like a real field to every check that came after it. It now discards what it does not recognise. So if your site is affected, updating is the whole fix. The leftover entry stays in your settings and is simply ignored from now on. One thing to know. If you clear a custom detail's name under Edit Names, that detail now disappears from the grid instead of showing under a name generated from its internal key. Nothing is deleted — typing a name again brings it straight back — and the public side of your site was already hiding such a field, so the two now agree.

A handler that stores booking information was listening to every save on the site rather than to bookings only. Saving an unrelated page or post could therefore write a booking status onto it. Nobody could reach data they were not allowed to reach — the check that was in place still asked whether you may edit that page — but the plugin was writing its own fields onto objects that were none of its business. Fifteen handlers across vehicles and bookings now confirm what kind of post they are writing to before they write. One of them was a live path that could attach vehicle ordering data to any post it was pointed at.
documents.s: Saving an ordinary page no longer writes booking data onto it

documents.t: When a screen's data failed to load, some screens showed a short "something went wrong, please refresh" message and others simply went blank — a white area under the WordPress menu with nothing explaining it. Every screen now shows the message, and a check keeps new screens from shipping without it.
documents.s: An admin screen that fails now says so

documents.t: Shared admin building blocks are now loaded from a common package rather than kept as copies inside Rentiva, and duplicated style declarations were consolidated. This was verified against a before-and-after comparison in both light and dark mode: nothing on your site renders differently. 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 were never published to the WordPress.org directory; everything they fixed is included here. The full history in both languages ships with the plugin.

If a guest booked with you first and created an account afterwards, the Customers screen could not see that booking. The customer's row read 0 bookings, their money never reached the summary cards at the top, and "View Bookings" showed an empty list. 6.1.4 fixes that, and it asks nothing of you: no database change, no re-saving of settings.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.4 — A booking linked by ID no longer vanishes from the Customers screen

documents.t: The screen reached a customer's bookings through the customer's e-mail address alone. That works for the ordinary case, where the account and the booking carry the same address. It fails for every case where they do not: a guest who booked, then registered later — the booking is attached to the account by its internal ID, not by a matching e-mail a customer who changed their e-mail address after booking an account added by hand that has no booking yet, or one known only through the plugin's own records In each of those, the booking was invisible to the screen. The row showed 0, the detail panel was empty, the summary cards at the top left that money out, and the account could be missing from the customer count entirely. Underneath the screen, four separate copies of "who counts as a customer" had drifted apart, which is why the customer list and the booking count could disagree about the same person. There is now one definition, and it is read from every place that asks the question — seven files across the plugin, twenty-nine call sites, including membership, counting, deletion and export. Those can no longer contradict one another. One note on how it was built, because it is the kind of detail that decides whether a fix is real: the query uses an EXISTS predicate rather than a widened join. A join that matches on either e-mail or ID counts a booking twice when both match. That was not assumed to be a risk — it was demonstrated by deliberately writing the naive version and watching the numbers double. The dashboard's own figures are computed separately and were not part of this change.
documents.s: The Customers screen now finds every booking

documents.t: Rentiva registers one top-level menu with a lot of pages behind it, and if you run a rental business you are inside those pages all day. The menu had been sitting below Appearance, Plugins, Users and Tools, near the bottom of the sidebar, so reaching any of it meant scrolling past the whole of WordPress first. It now sits directly below WooCommerce and above Appearance. That is as high as it goes: the position is the floor of the WordPress.org guidance that asks a plugin not to compete with WordPress's own top-level items, and Rentiva stays inside it rather than pushing above core.
documents.s: The admin menu is back above WordPress's own items

documents.t: Activating Rentiva across a network stopped at the hundredth site and skipped private sites entirely, so on a large network the sites past that point never got their tables. Both now get them. A subsite also reads its own language when building its URL slugs, rather than inheriting the network's.
Rolling a page back in the layout tool could write layout markup onto a completely different, unrelated post when a stale internal ID pointed at it. It can no longer touch a post it was not meant to.
documents.s: A layout rollback can no longer touch the wrong page

documents.t: On hosting with an external object cache, saving a customer, booking or vehicle left its list showing the old data until the cache entry expired on its own. The list now updates when you save.

The package no longer carries React source files that WordPress never runs. Where to get it. 6.1.4 is published on GitHub as v6.1.4. The WordPress.org plugin directory still serves 6.1.3 — submitting 6.1.4 there is a separate decision and has not been made yet, so updating from inside WordPress will not offer it to you today. The full changelog in both languages ships with the plugin.

If you run MHM Currency Switcher next to Rentiva, one click in Rentiva's database cleanup could wipe your products' fixed prices. 6.1.5 closes that, makes the cleanup refuse to delete anything it could not back up first, and fixes a Bookings filter that never finished loading. It is published on WordPress.org, so WordPress offers it to you as an ordinary update — nothing to re-save afterwards.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.1.5 — The database cleanup no longer deletes what is not its own

documents.t: Under MHM Rentiva > Settings > Database Cleanup, the invalid-meta cleanup treated every data key starting with _mhm as Rentiva's own. MHM Currency Switcher's keys start the same way, so the cleanup removed each product's fixed prices and, on stores whose orders are stored as posts, the currency, exchange rate and base currency recorded on each order. Keys under _mhmcs_ — Currency Switcher's — are now left alone. A key that only resembles the prefix is still cleaned.
documents.s: The cleanup only removes what belongs to Rentiva

documents.t: Three cleanups copy what they are about to remove into a backup table first: invalid meta, orphaned meta and old logs. None of them ever checked that the copy had actually been made. If the backup table could not be created, or could not be filled, the rows were deleted anyway — and the result screen still named a backup that did not hold them. Each of the three now deletes nothing unless both steps of its backup succeeded. It tells you why it stopped, and removes a backup table it created but could not fill. The old-log cleanup decides table by table, so the other tables are still cleaned. Two smaller faults in the same place are gone too: two cleanups started in the same second no longer share a backup table, and a long custom table prefix no longer breaks the backup table's name. A cancelled cleanup shows its own reason instead of "[object Object]". The Database Cleanup page in these docs now describes the tools with the labels you see on screen, including where the invalid-meta cleanup lives.

On the Bookings list, clicking the Pending chip could leave the page loading forever. The filter was built as a database query that grew with every detail stored on a booking; on a test site with real booking data the database was still working on it after 77 seconds. Every status chip now finds its bookings in one step, using the same rule the number on the chip uses — so the list and the number still agree. Filtering by licence plate now narrows a chip's list instead of replacing it. This had been there since 6.1.0.

Notices stay put. A notice such as the licence warning used to slide in under the page title a moment after most admin screens appeared, pushing the page down. It is now in place when the screen first shows. On Settings > Notification Templates it no longer appears twice, and on Settings it no longer turns into a pop-up that disappears after four seconds. The menu sits directly above WooCommerce, instead of below WooCommerce's Products, Payments and Analytics menus, so Rentiva's long list of screens stays in view. It is still below WordPress's own Posts, Media, Pages and Comments. Vehicle Settings > Display & Preview shows your first vehicle that has a featured image — its photo, name and daily price — instead of a grey placeholder and a sample car.
documents.s: Smaller things you will notice in the admin

documents.t: The search filter's "No vehicles found" message is now escaped on its AJAX path too, the vehicle edit screen no longer raises a PHP warning when the vehicle-details setting is empty, and unused e-mail screen JavaScript that called four admin actions that do not exist was removed. Where to get it. 6.1.5 is on WordPress.org and on GitHub as v6.1.5; both carry the same files. WordPress.org holds new versions for a few hours before sites are offered the update. Using Rentiva Pro? Pro 6.2.0 requires this version — update Rentiva first. The full changelog in both languages ships with the plugin.

6.2.0 gathers four weeks of work. Contact messages move to a screen of their own and their attachments to a private folder, the separate customer dashboard is retired in favour of My Account, and block and Elementor settings that were saved but never reached the page now take effect. It is published on WordPress.org, so WordPress offers it to you as an ordinary update. Using Rentiva Pro? Pro 6.1.0 or older stops with an error on the vendor panel beside this release — update Pro to 6.3.0 right after.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.2.0 — Contact messages get their own screen, the customer dashboard retires, and ignored block and Elementor settings now apply

documents.t: MHM Rentiva > Contact Messages is a new screen: statistics, New / Read / Replied tabs, a month filter, search, bulk actions, and a detail view with the sender's card and their other messages. You can reply by e-mail, mark a message as replied, and the menu shows how many are unread. Links to the old list and edit screens open the new one, and existing messages are marked as read once, on update.
documents.s: Contact messages get their own screen

documents.t: Contact-form attachments are now stored in a private folder, uploads/mhm-rentiva-private/contact/, under random names. They can only be downloaded through the administrator's Download button, and deleting a message deletes its file. On update, existing attachments are moved there and their old public addresses stop working; any file that cannot be moved is listed once in an admin notice. Attachments are capped at 5 MB. On nginx, add the deny rule from the privacy section of the plugin's readme: location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/mhm-rentiva-private/ { deny all; }. On Apache the folder ships with an .htaccess that denies direct access. Using a media offload plugin? Exclude the folder from it.
documents.s: Attachments move to a private folder

documents.t: [rentiva_user_dashboard], its block and its Elementor widget no longer render a dashboard. A logged-in customer sees one line and a link to My Account; visitors see nothing; administrators also see a notice asking them to remove it from the page. The block and the widget are hidden from the editors, and Shortcode Pages no longer offers to create the page. Customers find their bookings, favorites and payments on My Account. See Master account dashboard (retired).

Saved settings reach the page. Among them: the contact form's type, phone, company, vehicle, priority and attachment fields, theme and auto-reply (every form used to render as "general"); the vehicles list's Columns; the vehicle details "Ratings & Reviews" section, which now follows "Show Reviews"; the availability calendar's height. The defaults keep the old look, so a page only changes where one of these settings had been changed. Elementor style controls for vehicle cards, lists, grids, featured vehicles and the booking button now style the page — most of them matched nothing before. Colours or spacing you saved earlier but never saw may now appear. Block settings stick. A setting changed in the block editor and saved is no longer overwritten on every render. Settings that never did anything were removed from blocks, widgets and shortcodes. A saved value is simply ignored and the page renders as before. The shortcode pages in these docs no longer list them. Two shortcode attributes were renamed in practice: Featured Vehicles no longer reads show_book_button — use show_booking_button="0" — and Unified Search no longer reads layout — use search_layout="vertical". Search Results has a single Default Sort Order (default_sort) instead of Sort By and Sort Order.
documents.s: Block and Elementor settings that were ignored now apply

documents.t: Vehicle cards show a 3:2 image and the vehicle's real rating; a vehicle without ratings shows none, and the placeholder "★ 4.8 (120 reviews)" is gone. The booking button reads "Unavailable" when the vehicle is out of service, and otherwise follows the widget's text, then your global "Book Now Button" text. The booking form takes the same look and matches the vehicle details layout. Customers screen: Total Spent, Active, VIP and Avg. Spend count only completed or confirmed bookings, customers who checked out through WooCommerce show their phone and address, and a customer with two phone records no longer appears twice. My Account lists: Payment History page 2 can be reached again, and My Bookings and Payment History filter before paging, so a filtered page is full. Testimonials' "Load More" keeps the order, filters and display options. The front end no longer turns dark because the visitor's operating system is in dark mode; your theme and the plugin's own Dark Mode setting decide.

A vehicle's gallery and featured image accept only images the editing user uploaded or may use, and never a sensitive document. Gallery entries stored earlier are shown only when their origin is trusted. Attaching an image to a vehicle requires permission to edit that vehicle. A contact form's custom recipient (email_to) is used only while that address is still set on the page that holds the form; otherwise the message goes to the global recipient. The visitor's IP address is no longer included in the admin e-mail, and the contact form's type and priority are checked against the allowed values. The database cleanup no longer deletes Rentiva Pro's message-thread, commission-hold and vendor IBAN records.

Ten hooks and the customer dashboard classes were removed, including the mhmrentiva_dashboard_* filters and three mhmrentiva_availability_calendar_* filters; render_shortcode() and output_shortcode() remain as deprecated shims — use render_canonical(). New hooks include mhmrentiva_contact_recipient_fallback, mhmrentiva_gallery_attachment_allowed and mhmrentiva_retired_dashboard_notice, plus REST routes under mhm-rentiva/v1/contact-messages (administrators only). Three database steps run once on update: contact statuses, contact attachments and Elementor style ids. Where to get it. 6.2.0 is on WordPress.org and on GitHub as v6.2.0; both carry the same files. WordPress.org holds new versions for a few hours before sites are offered the update. Using Rentiva Pro? Update Rentiva first, then Pro to 6.3.0 — Pro 6.1.0 or older stops with an error on the vendor panel beside this release. The full changelog in both languages ships with the plugin.

6.2.1 is a privacy fix for sites that build pages with Elementor. Rentiva's Elementor widgets could leave the account data of the person who saved a page inside that page's stored text, where the site search could find it. This release stops that and cleans up the pages already affected. It is published on WordPress.org, so WordPress offers it to you as an ordinary update. If you use Elementor, update now and do the two steps under "After updating".
documents.s: Rentiva 6.2.1 — Elementor widgets no longer write the saving user's account data into a page's stored text

documents.t: When a page, post or template holding a Rentiva Elementor widget was saved, Elementor also stored a plain-text copy of it in the post content. The Rentiva widgets wrote into that copy what the person saving it saw: their bookings, payment history, favourites, e-mail address and security tokens. The site search reads that copy, so on a published page anyone could find this data.

Rentiva widgets write nothing into the plain-text copy Elementor stores when a page is saved. They also leave Elementor's markdown copy empty and are never stored in Elementor's shared element cache, even when a widget's Cache Settings is set to Active. Visitors see no change. The page itself still shows each visitor their own data.

After the update, a one-time background job rebuilds the stored plain text of every Elementor page, post and template that holds a Rentiva widget, drafts included, and drops its cached markdown copy. It runs through WP-Cron in batches of 50, retries pages that fail and waits longer between tries while it cannot make progress. It does not change a page's modified date or create a revision, so your pages keep their dates and history.
documents.s: Affected pages are cleaned up for you

documents.t: Purge your page cache, so cached copies of an affected page are replaced. Using a search plugin? Rebuild its index, so it forgets the old text. Optionally, clear Elementor's own cache under Elementor > Tools > Clear Files & Data. Older revisions Older revisions of an affected page still contain the old text. Only users who can edit that page can see them. Where to get it. 6.2.1 is on WordPress.org and on GitHub as v6.2.1; both carry the same files. WordPress.org holds new versions for a few hours before sites are offered the update. The full changelog in both languages ships with the plugin.

6.3.0 gathers the work since 6.2.1. Rentals get a site-wide deposit setting, a vehicle set to transfer only can no longer be rented, and Rentiva widgets show safe previews in the Elementor and block editors. E-mail settings that were saved but ignored now apply, and the booking form checks on the server what it used to take from the browser. No database step runs on update. 6.3.1 followed the same day with a fix for Elementor sites — see the end of this post. It is published on WordPress.org, so WordPress offers it to you as an ordinary update. Using Rentiva Pro? Update Pro to 6.4.0 right after.
documents.s: Rentiva 6.3.0 — A site-wide rental deposit, safe editor previews, e-mail settings that apply, and a booking form the server checks

documents.t: Settings > Payment has two new fields: Rental Payment Type (full payment or percentage deposit, default percentage) and Deposit Rate (%) (1–100, default 10). The defaults keep today's behaviour. The Payment tab is now always shown; it used to appear only without WooCommerce. Every price screen reads the same rate. A vehicle's own deposit rate still wins over the site-wide setting. An empty deposit field now follows the site-wide setting. It no longer means a fixed 10%, and the booking form no longer charges in full because of it. The vehicle field accepts 1–100 (it was capped at 50), and the edit screen names the site-wide value it falls back to.

A vehicle whose service type is "transfer only" no longer appears in the vehicle grid and list, search results, featured vehicles, the booking form, alternatives, the calendar's vehicle switcher or the manual booking list, and its page has no booking button. The server refuses a rental booking, quote or payment for it. Transfer bookings for that vehicle are not affected, and a vehicle with no service type stays rentable.
documents.s: Transfer-only vehicles can no longer be rented

documents.t: Rentiva widgets render inside a preview frame. Account widgets (My bookings, Favourites, Payment history, Vehicle comparison, User dashboard) always show sample rows with a "Preview: sample data" note — never your own account data. Vehicle details and the rating form show a sample vehicle when the page has none, and a clear note when the vehicle ID is wrong. Catalog widgets show your real public data. Forms in the editor are inert. One "Rentiva" category. All Rentiva blocks sit in a "Rentiva" category in the block inserter, and the Elementor widget category is renamed "Rentiva"; saved pages are not affected. The "MHM " prefix was removed from widget and block names. Elementor's "Parity Controls" section is now "Additional Settings", with translatable labels and options. Saved widget settings are unchanged. Block settings panels are translated. If a WordPress.org language pack is installed, its newer translations win, and strings the pack does not have yet come from the plugin's own translations instead of showing in English.
documents.s: Safe previews in Elementor and the block editor

documents.t: A template is sent only while its "Enabled" box is ticked. A template that was never saved counts as enabled, as the screen shows it. Previews and test sends ignore the box. The global booking and welcome e-mail switches now match the templates they name; before, they matched none. One cancellation e-mail. When a booking is cancelled, the customer gets the "Booking Cancelled" template (or the automatic-cancellation template when that one applies) instead of the generic status e-mail plus a second cancellation e-mail. If that template is disabled, nothing is sent. It now follows "Enable Outgoing Emails" and test mode like every other e-mail. The admin copy and admin alerts still go out, in test mode to the test address. The "Admin Email" fields are used. Booking alerts go to the address under Booking Notifications, refund alerts to the one under Refund Emails. An empty or invalid field still falls back to the site admin e-mail. Admin alerts that were sent directly now also respect test mode. Customer e-mails use the site language, even when the admin who triggers them uses another profile language. The "Booking Cancelled" e-mail's enabled box, subject and body are now saved, and the e-mail preview lists every template by its translated name and fills it with sample data. Booking e-mails show one booking number in the subject and the body (the order number when there is one), and the cancellation e-mail's account button opens the booking.
documents.s: E-mail settings that were ignored now apply

documents.t: The booking form checks on the server what the browser sends for the return time, required add-ons and the payment type. The return time is set to the pickup time on the server, so the priced period is the one blocked. Required add-ons are enforced and shown checked and locked. Only "deposit" or "full" is accepted as the payment type. Saving a booking in the admin uses the booking form's calculation. It no longer drops add-ons from the total, charges a fixed 20% deposit, ignores the weekend rate, or re-prices transfer bookings at the vehicle's daily rate. Editing a booking in the admin checks availability. Moving a booking onto taken dates, or re-confirming a cancelled booking whose dates were sold, is refused with a notice. A moved booking frees its old dates and holds its new ones. When the chosen vehicle is not free, the booking form shows the notice and suggested alternatives, and the booking button stays disabled until an available vehicle or dates are chosen.

Vehicle deposit fields: a vehicle with an empty field now follows the site-wide rate under Settings > Payment; one with its own rate keeps it. E-mail templates: a template whose "Enabled" box is unticked is no longer sent. Look over the boxes on the e-mail settings screen. "Admin Email" fields under Booking Notifications and Refund Emails: they are now used, so make sure they hold the right address. Drop-off location in the search form: it is hidden by default now; it only mirrored the pick-up location and nothing used it. Add show_dropoff_location="true" to the shortcode, block or Elementor widget to show it. Transfer-only vehicles disappear from rental listings and the booking form.

The customer's booking page matches the booking. Pending, cancelled and completed bookings get their own heading; the deposit shows as paid only after the payment arrives; "Pay Remaining Amount" waits for the deposit; pickup instructions appear only for confirmed bookings. The booking number is the same in the list, the dashboard and the detail, and it can be searched. Cart and order: each booking shows as the vehicle's name plus "rental" with the vehicle's image, each add-on is listed once with its price, transfers have no return-date row, and order dates use the site's date format. Booking form prices follow the store's currency position and thousand separator. Vehicle pages: the rating summary shows a bar for every star value (1 and 2 stars were missing); "Similar vehicles" is hidden when empty and no longer lists the vehicle itself; visitors no longer see raw [rentiva_login_form] text under reviews, and Register appears only when the site allows registration. Vehicle comparison shows default rows until you choose your own, and your first selection is saved. "Reset to defaults" on the Display tab restores the default fields instead of hiding them. Availability calendar: picking the same day for pickup and return opens the booking form with the pickup date filled instead of an error. Two calendars on one page no longer drive each other, and the vehicle dropdown works again. Settings that now stick: the default rental location on the Vehicle tab is saved, search uses its minimum rental days, the contact form uses the support e-mail from the General tab, and the e-mail header image field is visible. Translations: the Turkish translation was reviewed end to end, Turkish sites write percentages as "%20", and admin screens no longer show recently added strings in English when a WordPress.org language pack is installed.

Besides the booking form checks above: a vehicle title with an apostrophe no longer breaks the calendar's "Choose another vehicle" button, vehicle data in the availability calendar and the booking edit screen is always handled as text, and the lazy loader no longer loads remote content or scripts from data-lazy attributes.

New filters: mhmrentiva_cart_item_name, mhmrentiva_email_template_labels, mhmrentiva_email_preview_context, mhmrentiva_parity_labels, mhmrentiva_translation_dirs, mhmrentiva_render_context and mhmrentiva_settings_programmatic_keys. Add-ons can rely on DepositCalculator::resolve_rate(), VehicleDataHelper::get_service_type() / allows_service() / service_meta_query(), RenderContext, BlockRegistry::register_block() and CurrencyHelper::format_percentage() from 6.3.0. Util::has_overlap_locked() takes an optional booking to exclude. The content and script types of the data-lazy loader were removed, as was the unused mhmrentiva_booking_validation hook-up.

6.3.1 followed on the same day with two fixes: Elementor-built pages are found. A Rentiva widget, or a [rentiva_*] shortcode inside an Elementor widget, lives in Elementor's data rather than the page content, so Rentiva's page finder missed it: "Book now" buttons and other links fell back to the home page, and Shortcode Pages listed the page as missing. A page with the shortcode or block in its content still wins. On Elementor sites whose vehicle-details page is now found, vehicle pages move under that page, with a 301 redirect from /vehicle/..., as on block and shortcode sites. Translation tokens in notices now use a format WordPress.org's translation tool can check, and the Turkish catalogue uses the plural formula translate.wordpress.org uses. Where to get it. Rentiva is on WordPress.org and on GitHub as v6.3.0; both carry the same files. WordPress.org holds new versions for a few hours before sites are offered the update. Using Rentiva Pro? Update Rentiva first, then Pro to 6.4.0. The full changelog in both languages ships with the plugin.

MHM Rentiva v4.21.2 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, eklentinin ticaret ve operasyon yeteneklerini kökten değiştiren "Vendor Management", "Financial Architecture" ve "VIP Transfer" modüllerini beraberinde getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.21.2: Vendor Yönetimi ve Finansal Mimari Devrimi

documents.t: Bu güncelleme, MHM Rentiva'yı sadece bir rezervasyon motoru olmaktan çıkarıp, tam teşekküllü bir pazaryeri (marketplace) ve transfer yönetim platformuna dönüştürüyor.

Artık platformunuzda birden fazla tedarikçiyi yönetebilirsiniz. Her tedarikçi kendi araçlarını, fiyatlandırmasını ve rezervasyonlarını kontrol edebilir. Tedarikçi Paneli: Özelleştirilmiş admin arayüzü. Performans Takibi: Tedarikçi bazlı doluluk ve gelir raporları.

Ödeme yönetimi ve komisyon hesaplamaları tamamen standardize edildi. Commission Management: Esnek komisyon oranları ve otomatik hesaplama. Ledger System: Tüm finansal hareketlerin şeffaf bir şekilde kaydedildiği muhasebe defteri. Payouts: Tedarikçi ödemelerinin merkezi takibi.

Noktadan noktaya rota bazlı fiyatlandırma ve rezervasyon sistemi. Rota Bazlı Fiyatlandırma: Mesafe veya rota bazlı dinamik fiyat tanımlama. Transfer Rezervasyonu: Araç kiralama akışından bağımsız, optimize edilmiş transfer deneyimi.

Sadece özellik değil, altyapı olarak da güçlendik: Hardened REST API: SecurityHelper ve AuthHelper ile API uç noktaları daha güvenli hale getirildi. WP 6.7+ Uyumlu: En son WordPress sürümleriyle tam uyumluluk ve performans optimizasyonu. Modern Gereksinimler: Minimum PHP 8.1+ ve WP 6.7+ standartlarına geçiş yapıldı.

Tür Açıklama ✨ Yeni Modül Vendor Yönetim Sistemi (Multi-vendor desteği). 💸 Finans Gelişmiş finansal mimari, komisyon ve defter (ledger) sistemi. 🛫 Transfer VIP Transfer modülü ve rota bazlı fiyatlandırma motoru. 🛡️ Güvenlik REST API güvenlik katmanları (AuthHelper entegrasyonu). 🚀 Performans PHP 8.1+ optimizasyonu ve autoloader iyileştirmeleri. 🧹 Paketleme .distignore ile optimize edilmiş, tertemiz eklenti paketi yapısı.

Bu sürüm, mhm-rentiva ekosisteminde bugüne kadar yapılmış en kapsamlı modüler genişletmedir. Modüller arası veri bütünlüğü Util::has_overlap() ve DepositCalculator gibi merkezi sınıflar üzerinden garanti altına alınmıştır. MHM Rentiva hakkında daha fazla bilgi ve dokümantasyon için Doküman Sayfamızı ziyaret edebilirsiniz.

MHM Rentiva v4.23.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, vendor'ların transfer hizmetlerini şehir bazlı yönetebilmesini sağlayan yeni bir mimari, kapsamlı Dashboard widget denetimi ve onlarca hata düzeltmesi getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.23.0: Vendor Transfer Mimarisi & Dashboard Denetimi

documents.t: v4.23.0'ın en büyük yeniliği, Şehir → Nokta hiyerarşisi ile vendor'ların transfer operasyonlarını yönetebilmesidir: Şehir bazlı filtreleme: Her lokasyona bir şehir alanı eklendi. Vendor'lar yalnızca kendi şehirlerindeki lokasyonları ve rotaları görebilir. Rota bazlı fiyatlandırma: Admin'in belirlediği min_price — max_price aralığında her vendor kendi rota fiyatını belirleyebilir. Transfer arama motoru: Rota bazlı araç filtreleme ve vendor fiyatı desteği ile yeniden yapılandırıldı. Vendor fiyatı yoksa rotanın base_price değeri fallback olarak kullanılır. Veritabanı: DatabaseMigrator v3.4.0 ile lokasyonlara city sütunu, rotalara max_price sütunu eklendi.

Dashboard widget'larında kapsamlı bir denetim yapıldı: Timezone tutarlılığı: Geri sayım ve operasyon widget'ları WordPress timezone ayarına uyumlu hale getirildi. Cache invalidation: İstatistik cache key prefix uyumsuzluğu düzeltildi. WC email görselleri: Rezervasyon onay e-postalarında araç görseli artık doğru gösteriliyor. Tasarım iyileştirmeleri: 2x2 grid istatistik kartları, yerelleştirilmiş gelir grafiği, mesajlar widget'ı yeniden tasarlandı. Lite gating: Gelir Grafiği ve Yaklaşan Operasyonlar widget'ları artık Pro-only.

strtotime('') hatası: Boş tarih parametresi bugünün tarihini döndürüyordu, aktif booking'li araçlar hatalı filtreleniyordu. Guard eklendi. Lokasyon filtresi: Radio butonlardan checkbox'a dönüştürüldü; birden fazla lokasyon seçilebilir. Transfer tab doğrulama: Transfer alanları (origin_id, destination_id, date, luggage_*) hardcoded required olarak ayarlandı.

Ödeme günlükleri post_type uyumsuzluğu giderildi. Kayıt sayısı daima 0 dönen sorgu hatası düzeltildi. Geçmiş silme işlevi artık çalışıyor (transient tabanlı). Araç CSV/JSON PHP 8 strict types fatal error'ı giderildi.

Araç ruhsat doğrulama: Vendor araç ekleme formunda ruhsat bilgisi doğrulanıyor. Düzenleme formu: Vendor araç düzenlemesinde yeniden inceleme (re-review) mekanizması. Vendor rozeti: Vendor araçlarında tedarikçi rozeti görüntüleniyor.

Engellli tarihler: "Tümüne Uygula" AJAX düzeltmesi; tarayıcı verisi payload'da gönderiliyor. Elementor: 7 widget'ta attribute kontrol sayısı artırıldı (VehicleComparison, MyBookings, MyFavorites, VehicleDetails, Testimonials, VehiclesGrid, FeaturedVehicles). Ayarlar: Cache tekrarı, ölü ayarlar temizliği, SetupWizard sayfa listesi ve AssetManager guard düzeltmeleri. Çeviri: 15+ yeni Türkçe çeviri, WP 6.5+ .l10n.php dosyası yenilendi.

Tür Açıklama 🏗️ Mimari Vendor Transfer Lokasyon sistemi: Şehir→Nokta hiyerarşisi. 💰 Fiyatlama Vendor rota bazlı fiyatlandırma (min/max aralığı). 🔍 Arama Transfer arama motoru rota bazlı filtreleme + vendor fiyatı. 🗄️ Veritabanı v3.4.0 migration: city + max_price sütunları. 📊 Dashboard 11 hata düzeltmesi: timezone, cache, WC email, tasarım, Lite gating. 🔎 Filtre strtotime hatası, lokasyon checkbox, transfer tab doğrulama. 📅 Engelli Tarihler "Tümüne Uygula" AJAX düzeltmesi. 📤 Dışa Aktarım 4 kritik hata düzeltmesi. 👤 Vendor Ruhsat doğrulama, yeniden inceleme, vendor rozeti. 🎨 Elementor 7 widget attribute iyileştirmesi. ⚙️ Ayarlar Cache, ölü ayarlar, SetupWizard, AssetManager düzeltmeleri. 🌐 Çeviri 15+ yeni Türkçe çeviri, .l10n.php yenilendi. ✅ Test 567 test, 2036 assertion.

Bu sürüm, MHM Rentiva'nın vendor transfer mimarisini temelden yeniden yapılandırmıştır. Şehir bazlı lokasyon filtresi, rota bazlı fiyatlandırma ve Dashboard widget denetimi ile platform daha kararlı ve zengin bir yapıya kavuşmuştur. MHM Rentiva hakkında daha fazla bilgi ve dokümantasyon için Doküman Sayfamızı ziyaret edebilirsiniz.

documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.23.1: Vendor Form Yeniden Tasarimi & Sehir SelectWoo Migrasyonu

documents.t: Vendor ayarlar sayfasi (vendor-settings.php) sifirdan yeniden yazildi: Inline stil temizligi: Tum inline CSS kaldirildi, .mhm-vendor-form__* CSS sinif yapisi ile vendor-forms.css dosyasina tasinarak bakim kolayligi saglandi. Yeni alanlar: Hesap Sahibi (Account Holder) ve Vergi Dairesi (Tax Office) alanlari eklendi. Bildirim sistemi: Bildirimler artik mhm-vendor-notice siniflariyla gosteriliyor.

Vendor basvuru formunda onemli alan degisiklikleri yapildi: Hizmet Alanlari kaldirildi: Checkbox olarak sunulan Hizmet Alanlari (Service Areas) bolumu kaldirildi; yerine bilgi notu eklendi. Arac Sigortasi tasinidi: Basvuru formundan kaldirilip arac ekleme formuna ([rentiva_vehicle_submit]) tasindi. Yeni finansal alanlar: Hesap Sahibi (zorunlu) ve Vergi Dairesi (opsiyonel) alanlari eklendi. Meta senkronizasyonu: VendorApplicationManager ve VendorOnboardingController onay akisinda yeni alanlarin senkronizasyonu saglandi.

Tum sehir metin girisleri (<datalist>) modern bir secim bilesenine donusturuldu: Yeni mimari: <select> + WooCommerce selectWoo ile aranabilir, kullanici dostu sehir secimi. Yeni metot: CityHelper::render_select() — tum sehir secicilerde tek kaynak (SSOT). Guncellenen formlar: vendor-settings.php, VendorApply.php, VehicleSubmit.php, TransferAdmin.php. CSS/JS enqueue: UserDashboard.php, VendorApply.php ve VehicleSubmit.php dosyalarina SelectWoo asset'leri eklendi.

Arac ekleme formuna yeni bir belge yukleme bolumu eklendi: Arac ruhsatindan sonra sigorta belgesi (_mhm_rentiva_vehicle_insurance_doc) yuklenebilir. VehicleSubmit.php AJAX handler'i sigorta dosyasi isleme destegi ile guncellendi.

Kapsamli bir tasarim dokumani olusturuldu (docs/plans/2026-03-28-vehicle-lifecycle-management-design.md): Durumlar: Aktif / Duraklatildi / Geri Cekildi / Suresi Doldu Listeleme suresi: 90 gun, yenileme mekanizmasi ile Iptal ceza sistemi: Kademeli ceza puanlari Guvenilirlik skoru: 0-100 arasi performans degerlendirmesi Soguma suresi: Geri cekilmeden sonra 7 gun bekleme Tarih engelleme: Kotu niyetli kullanima karsi onlem 8 fazli uygulama plani hazirlandı

Hata Detay Arac durumu arama filtresi _mhm_vehicle_status arama sorgularinda kontrol edilmiyor — bakimdaki araclar arama sonuclarinda gorunuyor. Vendor askiya alma VendorOnboardingController::suspend() vendor'un araclarini yayindan kaldirmiyor.

Tur Aciklama Vendor Ayarlar Sayfa tamamen yeniden tasarlandi; inline stiller CSS sinif yapisina tasindi. Vendor Ayarlar Hesap Sahibi ve Vergi Dairesi alanlari eklendi. Basvuru Formu Hizmet Alanlari ve Arac Sigortasi alanlari kaldirildi/tasindi. Basvuru Formu Hesap Sahibi (zorunlu) ve Vergi Dairesi (opsiyonel) eklendi. Sehir Secici Tum datalist sehir girisleri SelectWoo bilesenine donusturuldu. Arac Formu Sigorta belgesi yukleme bolumu eklendi. Tasarim Arac Yasam Dongusu Yonetimi tasarim dokumani olusturuldu. Hata Kesfedilen 2 hata tespiti: arac durumu filtresi, vendor askiya alma.

Bu surum, vendor formlarinin modernizasyonu, sehir secici bilesenlerinin WooCommerce SelectWoo'ya tasınması ve arac sigorta belgesi yukleme destegi ile vendor deneyimini onemli olcude iyilestirmistir. Arac Yasam Dongusu Yonetimi tasarim dokumani gelecek surumler icin yol haritasi saglamaktadir. MHM Rentiva hakkinda daha fazla bilgi ve dokumantasyon icin Dokuman Sayfamizi ziyaret edebilirsiniz.

MHM Rentiva v4.24.0 sürümü yayınlandı! Bu sürüm, araçların tüm ömrü boyunca yönetilebileceği tam durum makinesi, vendor'ların araçlarını kendi kendine yönetebileceği AJAX self-servis uç noktaları ve adil rekabeti koruyan anti-gaming mekanizmaları getiriyor.
documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.24.0: Araç Yaşam Döngüsü Yönetimi & Vendor Self-Servis

documents.t: v4.24.0'ın ana özelliği: araçların Aktif → Duraklatılmış → Süresi Dolmuş → Geri Çekilmiş durumları arasındaki geçişlerini yöneten tam durum makinesi. 5 Durum: pending_review, active, paused, expired, withdrawn — her geçiş kurallarla korunuyor. Geçiş kuralları: Hangi durumdan hangi duruma geçileceği VehicleLifecycleManager tarafından zorunlu kılınır. Admin UI: Araç listesinde yaşam döngüsü sütunu, araç düzenleme ekranında meta kutu.

Araçlar yayınlandıktan 90 gün sonra otomatik olarak süresi dolar. Sona ermeden 10 gün ve 3 gün önce vendor'a uyarı e-postaları gönderilir. Günlük cron ile kontrol edilir; süresi dolan araçlar expired durumuna geçer.

Vendor'lar artık araçlarını admin müdahalesi olmadan yönetebilir: İşlem Açıklama Duraklat Aktif araç geçici olarak pasife alınır Devam Et Duraklatılmış araç tekrar aktifleştirilir Geri Çek Araç platformdan kalıcı olarak çekilir (ceza uygulanabilir) Yenile Süresi dolmuş araç yeniden aktifleştirilir Yeniden Listele Geri çekilmiş araç tekrar yayınlanır

Vendor'ların sık sık araç geri çekmesini önleyen kademeli ceza mekanizması: 1. geri çekme: Ücretsiz — ceza yok. 2. geri çekme: Aylık ortalama gelirin %10'u kesilir. 3. ve sonrası: Aylık ortalama gelirin %25'i kesilir. 12 aylık kayan pencere: Ceza sayacı 12 ay geçince sıfırlanır. Kesintiler doğrudan ledger'a kaydedilir, payout hesabından düşülür.

Vendor'ların fiyat manipülasyonunu önlemek için: Vendor iptal ettiği rezervasyonun tarihleri 30 gün boyunca yeniden bloklanır. Vendor düşük fiyatla almak için iptal edip daha yüksek fiyata satamaz. AntiGamingBlocker sınıfı bu tarih blokajlarını yönetir.

Tüm platformda vendor kalitesini ölçen 0-100 arası puan sistemi: Günlük cron ile yeniden hesaplama. Formül: İptal oranı, geri çekme sıklığı, duraklatma geçmişi ve tamamlanan rezervasyon sayısı bazlı. Admin kullanıcı listesinde vendor güvenilirlik sütunu eklendi. Araç kartlarında vendor badge olarak gösterilmeye hazır.

Yaşam döngüsünün her adımı için ayrı e-posta şablonları: Şablon Tetikleyici Araç Aktifleştirildi Araç active durumuna geçtiğinde Araç Duraklatıldı Vendor veya admin duraklattığında Duraklatma Devam Etti Araç yeniden aktifleştirildiğinde Araç Geri Çekildi Vendor geri çekme işlemi yaptığında Listeleme Süresi Doldu 90. gün sonunda otomatik 10 Gün Uyarısı Süre dolumundan 10 gün önce 3 Gün Uyarısı Süre dolumundan 3 gün önce Araç Yenilendi Süresi dolmuş araç yenilendiğinde Araç Yeniden Listelendi Geri çekilmiş araç tekrar yayınlandığında

Veritabanı: DatabaseMigrator v3.5.0 — mevcut tüm aktif araçlar için yaşam döngüsü durumu otomatik migrate edildi. Login Yönlendirme: wp-login.php erişimi WooCommerce hesap sayfasına yönlendirildi. documents.t: Özellik etiketleri taşma sorunu: Vites, yakıt, koltuk sayısı gibi spec chip'leri dar ekranlarda kart kenarından taşıyordu. Artık kart sınırları içinde kalıyor ve uzun etiketler doğru şekilde sarmalanıyor. Hibrit yakıt ikonu: Yakıt türü "hybrid" seçili araçlarda yanlış ikon gösteriliyordu. Doğru simgeyle değiştirildi.

Boş satır kaldırıldı: Takvim bileşeninin altında fazladan bir boş satır render ediliyordu — kaldırıldı. Kutu içinde kutu görünümü: Kenar çubuğunda takvim widget'ının kendi arka planı ile dış kart arka planı iç içe iki kutu izlenimi yaratıyordu. İç kaynağın arka planı nötrleştirildi, artık tek bir kart olarak görünüyor.

Araç görseli görünürlüğü: Form başlığındaki araç görseli açık arka planlarda düşük kontrasta sahipti. Altına bir degrade arka plan eklenerek araç her zaman görünür durumda tutuluyor. Kart başlık stili birleşimi: Rezervasyon formunun farklı bölümleri (tarih, müşteri bilgisi, ek hizmetler, fiyat özeti) birbirinden farklı başlık stillerine sahipti. Tüm bölümler artık aynı başlık tipografisi ve padding değerlerini kullanıyor.

Ödeme yöntemleri dikey: Çoklu ödeme yöntemi (kart, havale, kapıda ödeme) etkin olduğunda seçenekler yatay olarak sıralanıyor ve mobilde taşıyordu. Artık tek sütun, dikey stack — her ekran genişliğinde tutarlı. Kupon alanı ikon: "Kupon kodunuz var mı?" uyarı satırındaki ikon belirli tema kombinasyonlarında bozuk (kare/?) görünüyordu. İkon emoji ile değiştirildi, her temada render oluyor.

Rezervasyon meta satırlarında yeniden düzen: Rezervasyon detayları (tarih aralığı, ek hizmetler, teslim lokasyonu) daha önce tek bir cümle içinde virgülle ayrılmış şekilde gösteriliyordu — okunması zor. Artık her bilgi Etiket: Değer formatında ayrı satırlar halinde gösteriliyor. Ödemeye git butonu hover: Buton üzerine gelindiğinde yazı rengi arka planla aynı tonda kalıp okunamıyordu. Hover state rengi düzeltildi, yazı her durumda okunur.

Alan Açıklama 🔧 Araç Detayları Spec chip taşma + hibrit yakıt ikonu 🔧 Takvim Fazladan boş satır + kutu içinde kutu görünümü 🔧 Rezervasyon Formu Araç görseli degrade arka plan + kart başlık birleştirme 🔧 Ödeme Dikey ödeme yöntemleri + kupon ikon emoji 🔧 Sepet Meta etiket/değer satırları + ödemeye git hover

documents.s: MHM Rentiva v4.26.2: Tam Kaldırma Temizliği ve CLI Bootstrap Güçlendirmesi

documents.t: Önceden eklenti "verileri temizle" seçeneği ile silindiğinde 14 alt sistem tablosu veritabanında yetim kalıyordu: ledger, key_registry, commission_policy, payout_audit, tenants, usage_metrics ve eski alert/payment alt sistemlerine ait artık kullanılmayan tablolar. Bu v4.26.2 ile tamamen çözüldü. Yapılan iyileştirmeler: Tam liste: 27 özel tablonun tamamı kaldırma sırasında siliniyor Pattern güvenlik ağı: Listede olmayan ama mhm_rentiva_* önekiyle başlayan herhangi bir yetim tablo da otomatik yakalanıp siliniyor — gelecekte eklenen tablolar için güvence Kurtarma tablosu temizliği: DatabaseCleaner tarafından oluşturulan postmeta_backup_invalid_* geçici tabloları da kaldırma sırasında temizleniyor Tek kaynak prensibi: Silme listesi ve istatistik sayacı artık aynı kaynaktan okuyor — sayaç ile gerçek temizlik birbirinden uzaklaşamaz Savunma mekanizmaları: uninstall.php ve taksonomi temizleme adımı artık bozuk bir ayar kaydı veya eksik taksonomi nedeniyle sessizce durmuyor — hata yakalanıyor ve kalan adımlar çalışmaya devam ediyor Doğrulama: DemoSeed Docker ortamında v4.26.2 kaldırma testi → 0 tablo, 0 post, 0 ayar artık geride kalıyor. Tam temiz kaldırma garantili.

Önceden belirli koşullarda wp-cli komutları TypeError veya is_user_logged_in() undefined function hatasıyla çöküyordu. Kök nedeni iki yerde yatıyordu: SettingsCore::get() ve has() bir ayar kaydının dizi olmadığı durumda TypeError fırlatıyordu AdvancedLogger::log() WordPress tam yüklenmeden (örneğin early bootstrap'te) çağrıldığında is_user_logged_in()'i çağırıyordu ama bu fonksiyon o aşamada tanımlı değildi Çözüm: SettingsCore::get()/has() artık dizi olmayan bir ayar değerini tolere ediyor ve güvenli varsayılana düşüyor AdvancedLogger::log() plugins_loaded hook'u çalışmadan önce çağrıldığında erken return ediyor — log atlanır ama bootstrap çökmez Etkisi: wp plugin activate mhm-rentiva, wp mhm-rentiva * subkomutları ve diğer wp-cli akışları artık bozuk bir ayar kaydı ya da early-bootstrap log denemesi ile çökmüyor.

v4.26.2 ile şema migration'ları artık eklenti dosya sürümü değiştiğinde otomatik çalışıyor, WordPress aktivasyon hook'u çağrılmasa bile. Bu; manuel ZIP yükleme, FTP ile güncelleme ve wp-cli plugin update akışlarını kapsar. Önceki durum: Yeni tabloları oluşturmak için eklentiyi pasifleştirip tekrar etkinleştirmek gerekiyordu. Kullanıcıların çoğu bunu bilmediğinden "yeni özellik çalışmıyor" raporu geliyordu. Yeni durum: DB_VERSION sabiti değişir değişmez migration'lar sessizce ve tek seferlik çalışır. Aktivasyon hook'u hala destekleniyor — sadece artık zorunlu değil.

Tür Açıklama 🧹 Kaldırma Tüm 27 özel tablo (ledger, key_registry, commission_policy, payout_audit, tenants, usage_metrics + eski alt sistem tabloları) 🛡️ Kaldırma Pattern tabanlı güvenlik ağı (mhm_rentiva_* öneki) 🧹 Kaldırma postmeta_backup_invalid_* kurtarma tabloları 🔧 Kaldırma Silme listesi ve istatistik sayacı tek kaynaktan 🛡️ Kaldırma uninstall.php ve taksonomi temizliğinde savunma mekanizmaları 🔄 Güncelleme Şema migration'ları sürüm değişikliğinde otomatik çalışıyor 🐛 Düzeltme SettingsCore::get()/has() dizi olmayan değerleri tolere ediyor 🐛 Düzeltme AdvancedLogger::log() WordPress yüklenmeden güvenli dönüş
